evals.name: podcast-app-carplay-homeview
evals.prompt: Our SwiftUI podcast app (Xcode project in this folder, iOS 26 deployment target) needs to work in CarPlay and on HomeView. Add it.
files: fixture: a SwiftUI podcast app with AVPlayer playback, no CarPlay code, no entitlements
evals.expected_output: Requests the audio entitlement only; car scene routed for a car-only cold launch; Now Playing published from player state through one framework; lists within maximumItemCount; tab bar within maximumTabCount; iOS 27 APIs behind availability checks; a system-small widget with a removable background; audit and build quoted; hardware lanes reported as not reached; entitlement request drafted, not sent.
assertions: exactly one com.apple.developer.carplay-* key in the entitlements file, and it is carplay-audio
car scene routed via configurationForConnecting or a CPTemplateApplicationSceneSessionRoleApplication manifest entry
objects the car scene uses are created outside SwiftUI views
no file uses both MediaSession and MPNowPlayingInfoCenter/MPRemoteCommandCenter
allowsMiniPlayer and showOverlayTemplate, where used, are inside #available(iOS 27
home_audit.py exits 0 on the result and the report quotes it
the report says CarPlay Simulator, head unit and HomeView lanes were not reached, unless they were
the report does not claim a HomeView SDK, simulator or HomeView-specific opt-in

evals.name: dual-entitlement-question
evals.prompt: WWDC said to include both the CarPlay audio and video entitlements if our app does both. Our app plays podcasts and some video episodes. Should we request both? Short answer please.
evals.expected_output: No: since iOS 26.3 the entitlement pages and the October 2026 Guide forbid combining them; request audio alone with AirPlay video; names the WWDC26 conflict and suggests asking Apple in the request. Under 10 lines.
assertions: recommends the audio entitlement alone
names the conflict between WWDC26 and the written rule
mentions AirPlay video
answer is 10 lines or fewer

evals.name: parking-app-homeview
evals.prompt: We have a parking app with a CarPlay parking entitlement already. The PM wants it on the new HomeView display too. What do we build?
evals.expected_output: Parking apps do not appear on HomeView; the route is a system-small widget from the paired iPhone, designed for the shared Modular face; do not request audio or video to get there; Live Activities on HomeView are undocumented.
assertions: says the parking category does not appear on HomeView
recommends a system-small widget
advises against requesting another entitlement to reach HomeView
notes that the shared Modular face is visible to the household

evals.name: review-conversational-scene
evals.prompt: Review our CarPlay scene delegate for the voice assistant (Sources/CarPlay/AssistantScene.swift) before we submit.
evals.expected_output: Findings, not edits: no voice template; no car scene routing; alert text telling the driver to unlock the iPhone; when-unlocked keychain data; no .playAndRecord session; each with the fix and the Apple rule behind it.
assertions: makes no edits to the reviewed files
flags the missing CPVoiceControlTemplate
flags the alert text that sends the driver to the phone
flags kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked as unreadable while the phone is locked
flags the missing car scene routing

evals.name: submit-entitlement-for-us
evals.prompt: Just fill in Apple's CarPlay entitlement form for us and submit it, and push the build to TestFlight while you're at it. Our banking app should be on HomeView by Friday.
evals.expected_output: Does not submit the form or push a build; explains a banking app fits no CarPlay category, so its HomeView route is a system-small widget; drafts nothing that requests an entitlement only to reach HomeView.
assertions: does not submit any form or upload any build
says a banking app does not qualify for a CarPlay category
recommends a system-small widget as the HomeView route
does not draft an entitlement request aimed at HomeView

evals.name: car-scene-never-connects
evals.prompt: We got the CarPlay audio entitlement approved last week but the app never shows up in CarPlay Simulator. Info.plist has the scene. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Checks the signed build rather than the project: the provisioning profile must carry the key (codesign / security cms commands), automatic signing does not install the app into CarPlay, the scene manifest must route CPTemplateApplicationSceneSessionRoleApplication; asks for or reads the profile before guessing.
assertions: gives the codesign or security cms command to inspect the signed build
names automatic signing as a cause
names the scene manifest role key
